name: Request staff leave, route it up the configured chain, and have it reach attendance and pay
priorityReason: Attendance codes a day as leave from here, and payroll deducts unpaid leave from here. Neither works without it.

goal.capability: to request leave and know whether it is paid before I take it
goal.outcome: the absence is authorised, coded correctly in attendance, and paid or deducted according to what I had left

The off-day calendar is set, so a closed day is not consumed by the leave.

postConditions: The request carries its type, its dates and its reason, and its outcome is recorded either way.
The employee saw how much paid leave they had left before submitting, so they knew whether the days would be paid.
It went to the right approver for that employee under the configured chain, and nobody approved their own.
Approved leave is written into the attendance record and codes those days as leave rather than absent.
The paid allowance was reduced by what was used, and days beyond it are marked unpaid for payroll to deduct.
The employee was told the outcome, with the reason where it was rejected.

Closed days within the range were excluded and were not consumed by the leave.

businessRules.rule: Any employee may request leave. It is not a privilege of one classification.

The request is checked against the monthly paid leave allowance held on the employee's staff record, and the remaining paid leave is shown before they submit. An employee should know whether the days will be paid before they take them, not afterwards.
Nobody approves their own leave. The chain exists for that reason.

The request goes to the approver for that employee: staff leave to the School Admin, the School Admin's own leave to the Principal, and the Principal's leave to the Super Admin. The chain is configuration-based and the Super Admin can change it.
A rejection carries a written reason. An employee refused leave with no explanation cannot plan around it or appeal it.
Leave within the allowance is paid; leave beyond it is unpaid and is deducted by payroll. A single request may span both, and the days are marked accordingly.
Approved leave is written into the attendance record and codes those days as leave rather than absent. The two are treated differently by payroll and by any disciplinary process.
Days the calendar records as off-days or holidays are excluded from the leave and are not consumed by it. An employee should not spend leave on a day the school was shut.
The employee is told the outcome either way. A request that disappears is worse than one that is refused.
A request may be cancelled before its start date, and the allowance is restored. An employee who came in after all should not have spent leave.
A leave request cannot overlap one already approved for the same employee.
Approved leave makes the employee unavailable, which blocks a timetable assignment in that slot and is read when arranging cover.

transitions.condition: Approved. The days are written into attendance (BR-7).
Rejected with a reason. The allowance is untouched (BR-5).
Cancelled before the start date. The allowance is restored (BR-10).
The last leave day passes and the attendance is coded.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Excludes off-days from the days counted, and refuses an overlap with leave already approved.
Reads the monthly allowance from the staff record and shows how much paid leave is left, and how many of these days would be unpaid.
Sends the request to the approver for that employee under the configured chain, so nobody approves their own.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the request, the reason and the employee's remaining allowance, and approves it.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Writes the approved leave into the attendance record, coding those days as leave rather than absent.
Reduces the paid allowance by what was used, and marks days beyond it unpaid for payroll to deduct.
Tells the employee the outcome, with the reason where it was rejected.

alternateFlows.condition: The requester is the School Admin
alternateFlows.behaviour: Their own leave goes to the Principal, since nobody approves their own (BR-3, BR-4).
Their leave goes to the Super Admin, who also configures the chain (BR-4).

alternateFlows.navigation: Leave requests → Reject with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: The reason is recorded and the employee is told. The allowance is untouched and the days stay markable as ordinary attendance (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The request exceeds the remaining allowance
alternateFlows.behaviour: The employee is shown which days would be paid and which unpaid before submitting, so they know what they are choosing (BR-2, BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: The employee cancels before the leave starts
alternateFlows.behaviour: The attendance coding is reverted and the allowance restored, so somebody who came in after all has not spent leave (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The leave range spans a weekend or a holiday
alternateFlows.behaviour: Only the working days are counted, so an employee does not spend leave on a day the school was shut (BR-8).

departures.requirement: There is no route by which an employee approves their own leave, including where a configuration error would otherwise route it to them. Such a configuration is flagged rather than honoured.
The allowance is read from the staff record at the moment of assessment, so leave management and payroll can never disagree about what an employee is entitled to.
The paid and unpaid split is shown before the request is submitted, not after it is approved.
Leave requests and their decisions are retained 7 years, matching payroll records.

openQuestions.question: Does an unused paid leave lapse at the end of the month or carry into the next? This is the same open point raised on the staff record.
openQuestions.assumption: Lapses as modelled. It changes the balance every request is assessed against.

openQuestions.question: Is there a minimum notice period for a leave request, and is sick leave exempt from it?
May leave be requested retrospectively, for a day already taken?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and sick leave is usually taken before it is requested.

openQuestions.question: Is a supporting document ever required, as for student sick leave?
Who approves when the configured approver is themselves on leave?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and this is the case that stalls a request.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
